message.reasoning_content:
Describe the kernel. Key risks: tower representation, out-of-range mask, x=0 handling in tower (basis of 0 gives 0 encoded... norm=0? reciprocal=0 → inverse=0, ok). Bit shifts in Triton on uint32; <<4 of 4-bit value, &255 handled. Potential issues: _basis uses multiplication by columns[bit] on int — value is uint32, ok. Risk: decoded<<shift with shift up to 4 and &255 fine.

Real risk: the affine transform uses rotations of decoded (the inverse) — matches reference. Reference itself computes inverse of zero as... exponentiation gives 0 for x=0. Good.

Possible bug surfaces: norm/extension 9 tower math correctness; tower tables; masking in loads with .to(tl.uint32); resolve_neg; result.to(tl.uint8) truncation; answer computed as uint32 with <<4 could exceed 8 bits before XOR rotations but final &255? answer never masked to 8 bits after the loop — inverse | (high*reciprocal << 4) could be up to... _mul16 outputs 4-bit, so inverse is 8-bit, fine.

One subtle: `value = tl.load(...).to(tl.uint32)` — input is uint8, loads as uint8; fine. But other=0 handles out-of-range.

Record description update.
